metadata.notes: DeepSeek Harness TUI 0.8.1 advertises /model, but its handler saves only the default for later agents and does not change the current session model.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: no
daemon_capability: n/a
driver_capability: ready

## Scenario signal

The scenario requires two completed turns in one live session. Turn 1 must use model A. A user action must change the same session to model B. Turn 2 must use model B. The final model must be B, and cumulative tokens must include both turns.

## Agent capability

The installed DeepSeek Harness launcher is 0.1.5-rc.2 and the installed community TUI is 0.8.1. The TUI documentation advertises `/model` as an active-model switch. The shipped implementation does not complete that behavior for the current session. `attachSession` reads `defaultModel.currentSelection()` once and installs a local `ModelSelectionRef` with `current: selection`. The `/model` action later calls only `defaultModel.saveSelection({ provider, model })`. No code path assigns the new value to the installed `selected.current` reference.

The DeepSeek Harness default-model contract confirms the consequence. `currentSelection()` returns a detached object. `saveSelection()` stores the default for later agents. The contract states that an existing session keeps its selected route and that per-session selection belongs to the entry point. Therefore `/model` in TUI 0.8.1 changes the default used by a later session, but turn 2 in the current session remains on model A. This misses the load-bearing same-session model switch.

The binary string scan did not expose another model-switch surface. `dsh --profile tui --help` exposes only resume and agent-preset flags. A source search found `/model` only in the TUI overlay described above. A scan of the existing local DSH v3 transcripts found no `request/header` record with reason `change` and no model-selection notice. The transcript result is supporting evidence only; the source path is the decisive evidence.

## Daemon capability

This axis is n/a because the installed agent surface cannot produce the required same-session switch. For context, the DSH adapter can parse model fields from request/header, request/context, and assistant/message records. That hypothetical parser path does not make an absent agent behavior recordable.

## Driver capability

The driver is ready. The factory helper reports support for `send`, `slash`, `keys`, `wait_turn`, and `sleep`, which cover the TUI overlay and both turns. No driver primitive blocks the scenario. The pipeline freezes at the agent pillar.

## Unblock condition

Reassess after the TUI changes `/model` to mutate the current Agent's installed `ModelSelectionRef`, or after another shipped DeepSeek Harness CLI entry point exposes a same-session model switch.
caveats: Vacuous-pass condition: a future cell could pass while proving nothing if it checked only a saved default or the final model, because both turns could still use model A. A recordable replacement must require two distinct request-context models on one session and cumulative tokens after turn 2.
The TUI 0.8.1 README says `/model` can switch the active model, but the tagged 0.8.1 source and installed JavaScript disagree. This assessment follows the executed source path.
This verdict is version-specific. Re-probe the TUI source after an upgrade because DeepSeek Harness core already provides the mutable ModelSelectionRef mechanism that an entry point can use.

record_blocked=upstream documents the mismatch with the adapter capability catalog: DeepSeek Harness core has a traced model-selection mechanism, but the installed TUI entry point does not connect `/model` to the current session's mutable selection.

sources.note: Tagged TUI source: attachSession snapshots defaultModel.currentSelection into a local ModelSelectionRef; setActiveModel only calls defaultModel.saveSelection and never updates that local current selection.
Tagged TUI documentation advertises `/model` as an active-model switch, establishing the documentation/source mismatch.
Official DeepSeek Harness contract: currentSelection returns a detached object, saveSelection stores a default for later agents, and existing sessions keep their selection.
Installed TUI 0.8.1 implementation. Lines around attachSession install a fixed local selection; setActiveModel calls only saveSelection.
Installed 0.1.5-rc.2 package contract for detached currentSelection and future-agent saveSelection semantics.
